title: Wi-Fi networks are missing
symptoms: Wi-Fi is missing from Quick Settings
No wireless networks are listed
Wi-Fi toggle disappeared or airplane mode is on
possible_causes: Wi-Fi may be off, airplane mode may be enabled, or Windows may not detect the adapter.
diagnostic_steps: Check the Wi-Fi and airplane mode tiles.
If the Wi-Fi tile is missing, look for a wireless adapter in Device Manager without changing it.
safety: A missing adapter entry does not establish a hardware fault. Leave drivers and firmware alone during basic checks.
source_title: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows

title: Connected to Wi-Fi but no internet
symptoms: Connected to Wi-Fi with No Internet status
Websites will not load even though Wi-Fi is connected
No internet on multiple devices connected to the router
possible_causes: The local connection can be intact while access beyond the router, including service from the provider, is unavailable.
diagnostic_steps: Try a second website and check the same network on another device.
If multiple devices lose internet, investigate the shared connection before changing PC settings.
safety: A router restart interrupts everyone on that network. Avoid a network reset during initial checks.
source_title: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows

title: Wi-Fi drops during calls or streaming
symptoms: Wi-Fi disconnects during video calls
Wireless connection drops repeatedly when streaming
Weak Wi-Fi signal far from the router
possible_causes: Distance, interference, or a PC-specific connection problem may contribute.
diagnostic_steps: Watch whether the Wi-Fi status itself changes when the call freezes.
Compare the behavior closer to the router or against another device on the same network.
safety: Brief interruptions during a test are possible. A network reset removes adapter settings and can require VPN or virtual switch setup again. Reserve it for after basic checks.
source_title: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows

title: Cannot rejoin a saved Wi-Fi network
symptoms: Wi-Fi will not connect after the router password changed
Saved wireless network rejects the new password
Cannot join a known Wi-Fi network
possible_causes: The selected network or its saved profile may no longer match the router configuration.
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the network name and whether other devices can join it.
If only the saved profile fails, consider reconnecting after confirming you know the current password.
safety: Forgetting a network removes its saved connection profile. Enter the password only in Windows and never in chat.
source_title: Fix Wi-Fi connection issues in Windows

title: Wired Ethernet shows disconnected
symptoms: Ethernet cable is plugged in but Windows says disconnected
Wired connection shows network cable unplugged
USB Ethernet adapter has no link
possible_causes: A loose cable, faulty cable or port, or an adapter issue may prevent the wired link.
diagnostic_steps: Reseat both ends and check Windows Ethernet status.
If available, compare a known-good cable or another suitable router port while keeping other settings the same.
safety: Avoid removing the adapter driver or resetting the network as an initial test.
source_title: Fix Ethernet connection problems in Windows

title: Windows takes a long time to start
symptoms: PC is slow at startup or after signing in
Many programs open at login
Startup apps show high impact
possible_causes: Programs launched at sign-in may compete for resources.
diagnostic_steps: Review Startup apps and the impact column in Task Manager.
If an optional and recognized startup app is a likely contributor, change one at a time and compare the next sign-in.
safety: Leave security, accessibility, device, and work-managed components enabled unless their owner confirms the change.
source_title: Tips to improve PC performance in Windows

title: High CPU usage during a slowdown
symptoms: Task Manager shows CPU near 100 percent
Processor usage stays high while the PC is slow
A process uses most of the CPU
possible_causes: One application or background task may be occupying the processor.
diagnostic_steps: In Task Manager, sort Processes by CPU during the slowdown.
Check whether the load comes from an app you recognize and compare after closing it normally if safe.
safety: Save work first. Avoid ending unknown, security, or Windows processes.
source_title: Tips to improve PC performance in Windows

title: High memory usage with many apps or tabs
symptoms: RAM is nearly full
Memory usage stays high with many browser tabs
PC becomes sluggish when many programs are open
possible_causes: Running applications and tabs may be competing for available memory.
diagnostic_steps: Sort Task Manager processes by Memory and note which familiar apps are largest.
Close unneeded tabs or apps normally, then compare responsiveness.
safety: Save work before closing apps. Avoid memory-cleaner downloads.
source_title: Tips to improve PC performance in Windows

title: Disk activity spikes while Windows is slow
symptoms: Task Manager shows 100 percent disk active time
Disk usage is high and Windows stalls
Disks stay busy while applications load slowly
possible_causes: A process may be keeping storage busy. High activity alone does not mean the drive is full or failing.
diagnostic_steps: Sort Processes by Disk during the slowdown and look for a sustained pattern.
Note whether a recognizable background task is active and compare once it finishes.
safety: Avoid interrupting updates or ending unknown processes. Review the source of the activity before changing anything.
source_title: Tips to improve PC performance in Windows

title: One older application is slow or freezes
symptoms: Only one older program freezes after a Windows upgrade
One application hangs but other apps are responsive
An old app became sluggish after a Windows update
possible_causes: The installed application version may have a compatibility issue with the current Windows version.
diagnostic_steps: Check whether the issue is confined to that application.
Check the app publisher or Microsoft Store for a compatible version before exploring compatibility options.
safety: Save the app's data first. Use its official publisher and avoid compatibility downloads from unfamiliar sites.
source_title: Make older apps or programs compatible with the latest version of Windows

title: Low free space on the system drive
symptoms: C drive is almost full or has only a few GB free
Windows shows a low disk space warning
System drive has little remaining storage
possible_causes: Installed apps, personal files, or temporary data may be using most of the drive.
diagnostic_steps: Open Settings > System > Storage and note the space available on the system drive.
Review which categories occupy the most space before deciding what to move or clean up.
safety: Review the files involved and preserve backups. Do not delete system folders or unknown files.
source_title: Free up drive space in Windows

title: Review temporary files and Storage Sense
symptoms: Storage Sense or Temporary files uses a lot of space
Large Recycle Bin takes up disk space
Temporary files keep accumulating
possible_causes: Temporary files or retained Recycle Bin items may use space on the system drive.
diagnostic_steps: Open Storage settings and review the temporary-file categories or Storage Sense rules.
Confirm what the selected cleanup would remove before using it.
safety: Cleanup rules can delete Recycle Bin contents or files in Downloads if configured. Review these settings before enabling automation.
source_title: Manage drive space with Storage Sense

title: OneDrive files take up local disk space
symptoms: OneDrive folder fills the disk
OneDrive files show green check icons
Always keep on this device uses too much storage
possible_causes: Locally downloaded or pinned OneDrive files occupy disk space.
diagnostic_steps: Check file status icons in File Explorer and confirm sync has completed.
Consider freeing local space for a synced file you do not need offline.
safety: Free up space makes the local copy online-only. Confirm the cloud copy is accessible and keep offline copies of files you need offline.
source_title: Save disk space with OneDrive Files On-Demand for Windows

title: Windows Update needs more storage
symptoms: Windows Update says it needs more space
Update will not install because free space is too low
Feature update asks for an external storage device
possible_causes: Setup needs free space to unpack and install the update.
diagnostic_steps: Read the amount of space Windows Update asks for and check the system drive’s available space.
Review cleanup options first. Consider external storage only when Windows Update offers it.
safety: Keep important files backed up. Do not delete Windows folders or disconnect storage being used by Setup.
source_title: Free up space for Windows updates

title: Move large files to external storage
symptoms: Large videos or photos take up the drive
Need to move personal files to a USB drive
Free space by transferring large personal files to an external drive
possible_causes: Large personal files can occupy significant space on the system drive.
diagnostic_steps: Find large personal files in File Explorer and check available space on the destination drive.
Copy a small sample and open it from the destination before moving larger batches.
safety: Keep a verified backup and confirm the copied files open before removing any originals. Avoid moving installed applications or system files by hand.
source_title: Free up drive space in Windows

title: Windows plays through the wrong audio output
symptoms: No sound from speakers after plugging in a monitor
Audio plays through HDMI or the wrong output
Sound goes to the wrong headphones or speakers
possible_causes: Windows may be sending audio to a different output device.
diagnostic_steps: Open the taskbar sound output selector and check which device is active.
Choose the intended device if it is listed, then play a brief test sound.
safety: Start with low volume, especially with headphones.
source_title: Fix sound or audio problems in Windows

title: One application has no sound
symptoms: Only one app is muted while other apps play sound
Browser has no sound but Windows sounds work
An app's volume is muted in Volume mixer
possible_causes: The app may have a separate mute, volume, or output setting.
diagnostic_steps: Play audio in the affected app and check its own mute setting.
Open Windows Volume mixer and check the app's volume and output device if listed.
safety: Test at low volume and leave unrelated app settings unchanged.
source_title: Fix sound or audio problems in Windows

title: Microphone does not work in a call app
symptoms: Microphone works in Windows but not in the meeting app
Mic is muted or app cannot access microphone
Others cannot hear me in video calls
possible_causes: The selected input, mute state, or microphone permission may be wrong for that app.
diagnostic_steps: Check the physical mute control and test the intended input in Windows Sound settings.
If Windows detects the mic, check the calling app's input selection and its microphone access.
safety: Grant microphone access only to applications you intend to use. Managed devices may require an administrator.
source_title: Fix microphone problems

title: Bluetooth headset connects without sound
symptoms: Bluetooth headphones say connected but play no sound
Bluetooth headset is paired but speakers still play
Bluetooth audio output is silent
possible_causes: The headset can be paired while another device is still selected for audio output.
diagnostic_steps: Check the active output in Windows Sound settings.
Select the headset if available and test gently before considering a reconnect.
safety: Keep volume low. Confirm the pairing process before removing a device.
source_title: Fix Bluetooth connected but no sound issue on Windows

title: Audio stopped after an update
symptoms: Sound stopped after Windows Update
Audio driver problem or no sound after installing an update
Speakers disappeared after an audio driver update
possible_causes: An update may coincide with changed audio settings or a driver issue.
diagnostic_steps: Check whether the intended device is still listed and selected in Sound settings.
Compare the timing with Windows Update history and inspect the audio device status before considering a driver change.
safety: Avoid third-party driver utilities. Defer rollback or reinstall until basic checks are complete and recovery options are known.
source_title: Fix sound or audio problems in Windows

title: Laptop gets hot and shuts down during use
symptoms: Laptop overheats and shuts down unexpectedly
Laptop gets hot on a blanket or bed
Blocked vents and excessive heat under load
possible_causes: Blocked airflow or a cooling fault may contribute to excessive heat.
diagnostic_steps: Stop the workload if overheating or shutdown recurs.
Once the device has cooled, check whether external vents are blocked and whether it was used on a rigid, flat surface.
safety: Do not reproduce a shutdown to test it. Stop using the PC and seek service if there is smoke, a burning smell, or repeated heat-related shutdown.
source_title: How to Stop Computer and Laptop Overheating and Shut Down Issues

title: Fan stays loud while the PC is idle
symptoms: Fan runs loudly at idle
Fan runs at high speed even without gaming
Constant fan noise when no apps are open
possible_causes: Background processor load, obstructed vents, or a cooling problem may be keeping the fan active.
diagnostic_steps: Use Task Manager to see whether CPU load stays unusually high after startup activity settles.
Check that the outside vents have clearance. If the fan remains loud at low load, consider manufacturer support.
safety: Avoid opening the case or changing fan settings during initial checks.
source_title: How to Stop Computer and Laptop Overheating and Shut Down Issues

title: Short CPU temperature spikes in games
symptoms: Intel CPU temperature briefly spikes during a game
Temperature jumps during loading and then drops
CPU gets briefly hot as game load changes
possible_causes: Short temperature changes can accompany changes in processor load.
diagnostic_steps: If a trusted temperature display is already available, compare a brief spike with sustained heat or throttling.
Use the specific device or processor guidance for interpreting readings.
safety: Avoid a universal temperature cutoff. Stop testing if the PC shuts down or shows signs of physical damage.
source_title: Seeing Temperature Spikes when Playing Games on Systems with Intel® Core™ Processors

title: Measure stutter and frame-rate drops
symptoms: FPS drops or a game stutters
Frame rate becomes uneven during gameplay
Low FPS and stutter on an AMD Radeon GPU
possible_causes: Uneven rendering load may show up as changing frame rates or frame times.
diagnostic_steps: On a supported AMD system with AMD Software already installed, check Performance Metrics during a short repeatable game scene.
Compare frame rate and stutter in that scene before and after one reversible graphics setting change.
safety: The AMD overlay applies to supported AMD configurations. Avoid long stress tests or logging that captures private on-screen information.
source_title: Monitor Performance Metrics with AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition

title: A game runs on the integrated GPU
symptoms: Game uses integrated graphics instead of dedicated GPU
Windows picked the wrong GPU for a game
Game uses the power-saving graphics processor
possible_causes: On systems with more than one GPU, Windows may select a different graphics preference for that game.
diagnostic_steps: Check the game’s entry under Settings > System > Display > Graphics.
If Windows exposes both GPUs, compare the listed preference before deciding whether to change it for that game only.
safety: A high-performance GPU may use more battery power and increase heat. Leave other apps unchanged.
source_title: Optimizations for windowed games in Windows 11
